sentences.text:
08.10.2024 Order No.
02. 1. Heard.

2. At the instance of opposite party No.2, the F.I.R. dated 31.12.2022 in UPD, Cuttack Sadar P.S.
Case No.615 of 2022 for the offences under Sections 506/406/420 of I.P.C. came to be registered against the petitioner.
At the stage of investigation, the parties have settled their dispute.

3. The allegation against the petitioner is that the petitioner had made an impression that he is the owner of the property i.e. Mouza-Adalia, Khata No.633, Plot No.1070 of 2099 and offered the opposite party No.2 to purchase the same, for which, he had taken Rs.33,00,000/- as advance from the opposite party No.2.
Subsequently, the petitioner did not execute the sale deed in favour of the opposite party No.2 and cheated him.

Hence, the F.I.R.
4.
The petitioner and the opposite party No.2 are present in the Court and being represented and identified by their respective counsels.
They have also filed self-attested copies of their Aadhaar Cards to establish their identity, which are taken on record.

5. The petitioner and the opposite party No.2 have conjointly stated that they have settled their dispute and filed a joint compromise affidavit dated 10.05.2024 inter alia stating as under:-
<1. That there was a dispute regarding non-execution of sale deed and some financial disputes arises between the parties, for which the second party filed on 1CC case before the learned JMFC, (Rural) Cuttack which was registered as 1CC No.254/2022 and it was sent to the Cuttack Sadar Police Station U/s. 156(3) Cr.P.C. for registration Sunakara Dalai vs State Of Odisha And Another .... ... on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24289341/
1 of FIR and subsequently FIR has been lodged against the First Party U/s.
506/406/420 of IPC vide FIR No.615 dated 31.12.2022.
2.

sentences.text: That in the meantime Charge-sheet has been filed vide Charge-Sheet No.512 dated 04.08.2023 and basing upon the Charge-sheet the Learned JMFC (Rural) Cuttack had taken Cognizance U/s. 420 of IPC on 28.08.2023.
And summon has been issued to the First party for his appearance.
Pursuant to the said summon the First Party has been appeared through his Counsel and had filed a petition U/s. 205 of Cr.P.C.
Now the case is pending before the Learned JMFC (Rural) Cuttack for hearing and fixed to 17.05.2024.
3. That in the meanwhile the parties in this present deed of compromise have been settled their disputes amicably.

4. That in the meanwhile, i.e. during pendency of this present G.R. Case No.3597/2022 with the help and efforts friends, local villagers and well-wishers the informant and the present petitioner, they are agreed to file this compromise petition supported by an affidavit.
In the said compromise petition the informant (Second Party) and the First Party following conditions as mentioned.
A. That the Second Party does not want to proceed with the present case further against the First Party.
B. That the First Party did not threaten nor having any enmity against the informant (Second Party).
C. That this application is being filed by the parties voluntarily after a long deliberation and thought and without force and coercion from anybody.
D. That there is no collision between the parties and this application is filed out of their own free will and violation.
E. That the informant wants to drop the entire criminal proceeding against the present petitioner.

F.
That the informant on his free will and without coercion wants to compromise with the present petitioner and does not want to proceed with the above noted criminal case against the present petitioner.
5. That it is humbly submitted here that the First Party and the informant (Second Party) are known to each other and there is no other disputes between the parties after the matter was settled.

Thus the informant (Second Party) does not want to proceed with this case.=
6.
On query from the Court, the opposite party No.2/informant has stated that he is completely satisfied with the terms of settlement and he has received the due amount.
Therefore, he does not want to proceed with the case against the petitioner.

7. Mr. Patra, learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State submits that since the parties have settled their dispute and present in the Court, there is no legal impediment in quashing the F.I R.

Regard being had to the fact that the parties have settled their dispute and the terms of settlement and keeping in view the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another reported in 2012 (10) SCC 303 and B.S. Joshi & others vs. State of Haryana &
another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675, I am of the considered view that subjecting the petitioner to trial would be a futile exercise.

Cuttack in G.R. Case No.3597 of 2022 arising out of 1.C.C. Case No.254 of 2022 and the consequential proceedings arising therefrom qua the petitioner are quashed.
10.
The CRLMC is accordingly disposed of.
